overview: Galan Lithium is an ASX-listed lithium brine developer whose flagship asset is the 100%-owned Hombre Muerto West (HMW) project in Catamarca Province, Argentina, located on the same salar as Rio Tinto's El Fenix/Sal de Vida and POSCO's Sal de Oro operations. During FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) Galan completed construction and commissioning of HMW Phase 1, produced its first processed lithium chloride, and transitioned from an exploration/development company into an early-stage lithium producer, with first product sales now targeted for Q4 CY2026 and nameplate production (4ktpa LCE, expanding to 5.2ktpa) targeted through CY2027. The company also holds the Candelas brine project (adjacent to HMW), the Greenbushes South hard-rock exploration tenements in Western Australia (adjacent to the world's largest spodumene mine), and a dormant 50/50 Canadian lithium JV with Redstone Resources.

business_model.summary: Pre-revenue through FY2026 - Galan has recorded zero sales in every reported period (FY2018-FY2026) and has funded exploration, construction and operations entirely through equity raises (no debt; debt/equity 0.0). The business model going forward is to mine and concentrate lithium-bearing brine at HMW into a 6% lithium chloride (LiCl) concentrate, sold under a binding offtake agreement to Authium (a US-based processing/offtake partner) which also funds, supplies and operates the nanofiltration plant at HMW in exchange for the product. Net loss widened from $9.3m (FY2025, restated $23.6m after including previously-capitalised Argentina admin costs) to $25.1m in FY2026 as the company moved from capitalising project costs to expensing operating costs during ramp-up. Capex fell from $74.7m (FY2024 peak) to $30.0m (FY2026) as Authium absorbed the ~A$65.5m cost of the processing plant.

revenue_streams.name: Lithium chloride concentrate sales to Authium (6-12 year offtake, 45kt LCE total)
revenue_streams.trend: not yet started - first sales targeted Q4 CY2026

revenue_streams.name: Offtake prepayment facility drawdown (Authium, up to US$6m)
revenue_streams.trend: available from first processed lithium, not yet drawn at FY2026 year end

business_model.customer_type: B2B - single offtake customer (Authium) for all currently contracted HMW Phase 1 volume; no retail/end-consumer exposure
business_model.geographic_mix: Asset base: 100% HMW and Candelas brine projects in Catamarca Province, Argentina; Greenbushes South hard-rock exploration in Western Australia; 50% interest in Taiga/Camaro/Hellcat lithium projects in James Bay, Quebec, Canada (JV with Redstone Resources, currently dormant). Corporate head office in Perth, Australia. No revenue geography yet exists.

main_competitors: Rio Tinto (Arcadium Lithium's El Fenix/Fenix and Sal de Vida, same Hombre Muerto salar)
Allkem legacy brine assets now under Rio Tinto
ASX-listed hard-rock peers for Greenbushes South exposure: Pilbara Minerals, IGO/Tianqi (Greenbushes), Liontown Resources
competitive_position.market_position: Pre-production developer at the smaller end of the Hombre Muerto basin's resource holders; HMW's 9.5Mt LCE total resource (combined with Candelas) is a genuine tier-1 scale brine asset, but Galan is years behind basin neighbours Rio Tinto and POSCO in reaching commercial production and lacks their balance-sheet scale, in-house processing technology and marketing networks

moat_factors.description: 9.5Mt LCE total mineral resource (HMW 7.87Mt LCE + Candelas 1.63Mt LCE) with average brine grades around 880-900mg/L Li, sitting in the same high-grade Hombre Muerto basin as Rio Tinto and POSCO's established operations; DFS-level economics described by management as first-quartile on the global cost curve

HMW was approved in 2025 for Argentina's RIGI large-investment incentive regime, securing a reduced 25% corporate tax rate, 30-year fiscal stability on tax/royalties/export duties, preferential FX access for imports and dividend repatriation, and customs/tariff exemptions - a structural advantage over projects without RIGI status and a direct mitigant to historical Argentine sovereign risk

The Authium agreement shifted ~A$65.5m of nanofiltration plant capex and operating risk off Galan's balance sheet in exchange for committing 45kt LCE of product and a 6-12 year offtake - reduces near-term funding risk but creates a single-counterparty dependency and cedes some margin/control over the core processing step

moat_factors.factor: Low-cost brine chemistry vs hard rock
moat_factors.description: Brine evaporation is typically lower capital intensity than spodumene hard-rock mining and conversion, and lithium chloride is directly usable as an LFP battery precursor, which management positions as an advantage versus spodumene-based peers

weaknesses: No revenue history and no proven ability to operate a commercial lithium plant - Phase 1 ramp-up has already slipped from H1 2026 to H2 2026 to Q4 CY2026 guidance, with management citing a severe Puna winter
Single-project (effectively single-country, single-province) cash-flow concentration until Candelas/Greenbushes South are developed, which is itself many years away
Switched processing technology from the DFS's chemical liming/filtration method to third-party nanofiltration without full commercial-scale validation at HMW
Reliant on one offtake counterparty (Authium) for the entirety of currently contracted Phase 1 volume

Long history of shareholder dilution - shares on issue have grown roughly 24x since FY2018 (~48m to ~1.14bn weighted average by FY2026), with further raises in FY2026 alone ($20m to Clean Elements Fund, $40m institutional placement)

growth_drivers: Ramp-up of HMW Phase 1 to nameplate 4ktpa LCE (targeted H1 CY2027) and delivery of first product sales (targeted Q4 CY2026), the key near-term re-rating catalyst from developer to cash-generative producer
Phase 1 expansion to 5.2ktpa LCE, funded by the January 2026 A$40m placement, with pond construction starting in the September 2026 quarter and higher volumes expected from H2 CY2027

Multi-decade phased build-out plan toward an eventual 60ktpa LCE at the conclusion of Phase 4, incorporating the Candelas resource (1.6Mt LCE, increased >150% in January 2025) to mitigate funding/execution risk via staged expansion

Greenbushes South exploration (new Exploration Licence E70/4889 granted in FY2026, WA government co-funded airborne gravity survey) adjacent to the Tier-1 Greenbushes hard-rock lithium mine, offering optionality beyond the Argentine brine business
RIGI fiscal/FX certainty removing a key historical barrier to investment and project financing in Argentina, potentially supporting further capital raising or debt financing on improved terms

Structural lithium demand growth from EVs and grid storage, with lithium chloride feeding directly into LFP battery precursor chemistry (the dominant battery chemistry globally) and some banks (e.g. UBS) forecasting persistent deficits through 2026-H1 2027

business.description: First product sales guidance has already slipped from H1 2026 to H2 2026 to Q4 CY2026; nameplate 4ktpa is not targeted until H1 CY2027, and brine evaporation ramp-up is weather-dependent and can be disrupted by abnormal conditions (as occurred in 2017)

Galan switched from the DFS-contemplated chemical liming/filtration process to Authium's nanofiltration technology; while tested with positive results, it is unproven at full commercial scale at HMW and any issue could affect permitting (EIA submissions) as well as output

All currently committed Phase 1 volume (45kt LCE) is contracted to a single buyer, Authium; non-performance or attempted renegotiation - explicitly flagged by the company as more likely in a soft lithium pricing environment - would directly hit revenue
Near-term financial performance depends entirely on HMW in Catamarca Province; the company has no other near-term source of cash flow

financial.description: No debt currently, but the company has relied on continuous equity issuance (shares outstanding up ~24x since FY2018) and explicitly flags that further financing may be required if ramp-up costs, timelines or the 5.2ktpa expansion exceed current estimates
Future lithium chloride sales will be USD-denominated while Galan's costs/reporting are in AUD and Argentine operating costs in ARS, exposing margins to AUD/USD and ARS/USD volatility
Despite RIGI's preferential FX access for imports and dividend repatriation, Argentina's broader currency and capital repatriation controls remain a live risk factor per the FY2026 annual report

regulatory.description: The RIGI incentive regime (25% tax rate, 30-year fiscal stability) was only approved for HMW in mid-2025 under the current Argentine government's reform agenda; any future change in government policy or legislation affecting RIGI could alter the project's tax, royalty and FX treatment

Adoption of nanofiltration technology requires inclusion in periodic EIA submissions under Argentina's DIA permitting regime, creating a title/tenure risk pathway if approvals are delayed or conditioned
Exposure to evolving environmental and climate-change-related regulation in both Australia and Argentina, including water use and community/biodiversity obligations at HMW

macro.description: Market commentary is split: some (e.g. UBS) see persistent deficits into 2026-H1 2027, while others (Rothschild & Co Redburn, Chinese futures market moves in mid-2026) warn that elevated 2026 production and mine restarts could create a 2027 glut just as Galan ramps into commercial sales
Chinese EV, battery and lithium chemical conversion demand and policy (e.g. battery consumption tax changes) heavily influence global lithium pricing, Galan's ultimate end-market reference price
Economic, social and political instability, inflation and sovereign risk in Argentina remain structural considerations even with RIGI protections in place

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Lithium market views are bifurcated: bullish banks (e.g. UBS) forecast 14-16% demand growth in 2026-2027 and a persistent deficit into H1 2027 on EV/ESS demand, while bearish commentary points to a 2027 oversupply risk as restarted and new mines (including Chinese lepidolite capacity) ramp up; S&P Global's 2026 balance (~1.48Mt LCE demand vs ~1.58Mt LCE supply) implies only a narrow surplus near-term. Brine producers like Galan sit toward the lower end of the global cost curve, offering some insulation versus higher-cost hard-rock supply in a downturn.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Highly cyclical commodity business; Galan's own share price and financing conditions have moved sharply with lithium sentiment, and the company is entering commercial production just as the market debates a potential 2027 supply glut
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no debt), but indirect sensitivity via the cost and availability of future equity capital and the broader risk appetite for pre-revenue resource developers
macro_factors.currency_exposure: AUD reporting currency, USD-denominated lithium pricing and offtake payments, and ARS-denominated Argentine operating costs create multi-currency translation and repatriation risk, partially mitigated by RIGI's preferential FX access for imports and dividends
key_input_costs: Diesel/power for brine pumping and evaporation operations
Nanofiltration consumables/reagents (supplied under the Authium agreement)
Skilled labour and contractor costs in remote Catamarca Province
Equipment and plant imports (partially eased by RIGI customs/tariff exemptions)

recent_developments.event: Signed definitive offtake and operating agreements with Authium: 45kt LCE lithium chloride concentrate offtake over 6-12 years, Authium to fund/supply/commission/operate the HMW nanofiltration plant, plus access to up to US$6m in offtake prepayments
Completed $20m placement to strategic investor Clean Elements Fund in two $10m tranches (1 September and 5 November 2025), funding completion of HMW Phase 1 construction

Received RIGI (Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones) approval for HMW - the sixth project and second mining project to receive RIGI status in Argentina, following Rio Tinto's Rincon project - locking in a 25% corporate tax rate and 30-year fiscal/FX stability
Announced a further A$40m institutional placement at $0.41/share to fund the Phase 1 expansion from 4ktpa to 5.2ktpa LCE, working capital, and Greenbushes South exploration
HMW Phase 1 construction reported ~92% complete, nanofiltration plant delivered to site
Commissioning complete; first processed lithium chloride produced at HMW, marking the company's transition from developer to lithium producer
FY2026 results: net loss $25.1m (FY2025 restated: $23.6m); cash $35.5m (FY2025: $4.4m); capex $30.0m (down from $74.7m in FY2024 peak); zero lost-time injuries for the year, down from four in FY2025

Project update narrowed first lithium chloride concentrate sales guidance to Q4 CY2026 (from H2 2026), attributing the slower ramp to a severe Puna winter; pond construction for the 5.2ktpa expansion to begin in the September 2026 quarter, with higher volumes expected H2 CY2027

Shares traded in the ~$0.23-$0.32 range, well below the $0.41 institutional placement price set in January 2026, reflecting market caution around the slipped production timeline and broader lithium price volatility

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report (30 June 2026) / September 2026 quarterly project update

items.notes: Slipped from H1 CY2026 (original) to H2 CY2026 (FY2026 Annual Report) to Q4 CY2026 specifically (September 2026 update); management attributes the delay to a severe Puna winter affecting evaporation/ramp rates
Dependent on successful stabilisation of the ramp-up from the ~9,000-10,000t LCE brine inventory already built in HMW's evaporation ponds

items.notes: Expansion capacity funded and scheduled but execution/timing not yet proven

items.notes: Company states the phased approach is designed to mitigate funding and execution risk versus building to full scale at once

items.target: $35.5m at 30 June 2026 (vs $4.4m at 30 June 2025 and $14.9m at 31 December 2025)

guidance.management_commentary: Management (MD Juan Pablo Vargas de la Vega) frames FY2026 as the year Galan transitioned from explorer/developer to lithium producer, citing completed Phase 1 construction, commissioning of the nanofiltration plant and first processed lithium chloride as key proof points. The company notes that all material assumptions underpinning the Phase 1 production target (per the July 2023 DFS) continue to apply and have not materially changed, while acknowledging that the ramp-up to nameplate and delivery of first sales are subject to factors beyond its control, including weather. No formal revenue, margin or EPS guidance has been issued given the company remains pre-revenue.

bull_case: Tier-1 scale, high-grade brine resource (9.5Mt LCE combined HMW/Candelas) in the same world-class Hombre Muerto basin as Rio Tinto and POSCO's established operations, with management citing first-quartile global cost-curve positioning

HMW has moved from developer to producer during FY2026 - construction complete, plant commissioned, first lithium chloride produced - de-risking the story relative to pure pre-construction peers, with first sales targeted imminently (Q4 CY2026)
RIGI approval locks in a 25% corporate tax rate and 30-year fiscal/FX stability, directly addressing the historically largest risk (Argentine sovereign/currency risk) in the investment case

Authium partnership shifted roughly A$65.5m of processing-plant capex and operating risk off Galan's balance sheet while still securing a 45kt LCE offtake and up to US$6m in prepayment facility - preserves cash and reduces funding risk through the ramp-up

No debt and $35.5m cash at FY2026 year end (post two 2025/2026 raises) provides runway through the ramp-up without immediate need for further dilutive financing, with Candelas and Greenbushes South offering multi-decade optionality beyond Phase 1
bear_case: Still pre-revenue as of FY2026 year end with a track record of slipping production guidance (H1 2026 to H2 2026 to Q4 CY2026) - the ramp-up to nameplate and first sales are unproven and weather-dependent

Extreme historical shareholder dilution (shares on issue up ~24x since FY2018) with two more large raises in FY2026 alone; the company explicitly flags that further capital may be required if costs or timelines slip further

Single-project, single-country cash-flow concentration in Argentina's Catamarca Province, with all currently committed offtake volume tied to one counterparty (Authium) whose non-performance or renegotiation risk is heightened in a soft lithium pricing environment
Switched to an unproven-at-scale nanofiltration processing technology from the original DFS chemical process, adding technical execution risk right as the company tries to hit nameplate rates

Lithium price outlook for 2027 is genuinely contested, with some forecasters warning of a supply glut from restarted capacity just as Galan ramps into commercial sales; shares were trading well below the $0.41 January 2026 institutional placement price through October/November 2026, suggesting the market remains skeptical of near-term execution
